title: Servepath Latency Strata Inspector: p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs non-streaming cohort overlays
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description: Goal: Build a Servepath Latency Strata Inspector dashboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency broken down by model and route with an explicit streaming vs non-streaming cohort overlay. This dashboard should make it easy for SREs and platform owners to: (1) quickly identify whether latency regressions are concentrated in streaming or non-streaming paths, (2) correlate latency spikes with trace-sampled waterfall captures, network/chunking events, and KV cache hit rates, and (3) enable focused follow-ups (rollbacks, model fallbacks, autoscale tweaks).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dashboard exposes p50/p95/p99 over selectable intervals (1h/6h/24h/7d) for each model x route. 2) A toggle splits the view into streaming vs non-streaming cohorts and overlays both cohorts on the same chart plus separate sparklines. 3) Each cohort point links to a trace sampler query and a representative example trace waterfall. 4) Panel shows cohort-level auxiliary signals: KV cache hit rate, average token batch size, request-size distribution, and tail error rate. 5) Alerting rules for sustained >20% p95 increase over baseline with automatic inclusion of top 3 correlated signals. 6) Dashboard documented in Console runbook and shipped with a rollout plan.
implementation_notes: Telemetry: extend existing latency metric to tag requests with servepath.io_mode={streaming,blocking} and servepath.model_route=. Ensure metric cardinality is bounded by only emitting 'io_mode' and 'model_route' values when route is in our catalog (use allowlist). Traces: add a dashboard-level sample_link generator that constructs a trace query trace.service:servepath AND trace.tags.model_route: AND trace.tags.io_mode:streaming. Metrics pipeline: add a lightweight aggregator to precompute percentiles (p50/p95/p99) via our metrics ingestion (compatible with current Prometheus/Clickhouse hybrid). For streaming, emit a per-chunk latency and a per-request aggregated latency so we can show both chunk-level and end-to-end views.
dashboard_panels: 1) Strata timeline: dual-axis p95/p50 line chart with streaming vs non-streaming overlay. 2) Cohort sparklines: small multiples per model_route with color-coded io_mode. 3) Waterfall sample panel: top 3 trace links for the selected time window (with synthetic golden trace comparison). 4) Correlated signals: stacked bar showing KV cache hit rate, average batch size, average request tokens, and tail error rate. 5) Anomaly heatmap: cells are model_route x hour showing percentile spikes. 6) Drilldown table: top slow request samples with request shape, io_mode, cache_hit, and link to original request payload (redacted).
queries_and_alerts: Example percentile query pseudo: METRICS.aggregate('latency_ms', by=['model_route','io_mode'], agg=['p50','p95','p99'], window='5m'). Example alert: ALERT if p95(model_route, last_15m) > baseline_p95*1.2 for 3 consecutive windows AND traffic_volume > 100 reqs/15m. When alert fires attach top correlated signals via correlation job. Alert should open runbook with first-run checklist.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - Chose precomputed percentiles in ingestion to keep dashboard responsive; tradeoff: slightly delayed resolution (30s-60s) vs live raw histograms. - To avoid cardinality explosion we only allowlisted model_route values; consequence: new routes require a small config update. - Streaming chunk-level metrics add extra ingestion cost; initial rollout will enable chunk metrics for 10 highest-traffic models only and evaluate cost impact.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: metric cardinality leads to ingestion cost spikes. Mitigation: enforce allowlist and sample low-volume routes. Risk: traces may not be sampled for short tail spikes. Mitigation: implement targeted trace-as-you-go capture triggered by alert and a temporary increase in sampling for affected route+io_mode.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable dashboard for infra and SREs for 2 weeks with 10 high-traffic routes; collect feedback. Phase 2: expand to all allowlisted routes and add automated alerting. Phase 3: expose read-only to PMs/product owners with contextual links. Postmortem & cost review after 30 days.
